builds.name: Reference: Ranked mid core
builds.goal: Reference for Aurora: the core and runes ranked Emerald+ mid players use most (3,082 ranked Emerald+ games with this core on OP.GG, patch 16.20, 51.9% win rate).
builds.hypothesis: A mobile spell skirmisher who repeats hits to extract healing spirits and uses hops to adjust short-range pressure. Her ultimate creates a movement zone rather than guaranteeing enemies remain trapped. The current mid provider core anchors this plan; later slots are observed options or reviewed kit completions. Core in purchase order: Stormsurge → Shadowflame → Rabadon's Deathcap. Electrocute keystone as played in those games. Remaining slots: Sorcerer's Shoes, Void Staff, Zhonya's Hourglass.
builds.summary: The proven mid baseline: Stormsurge → Shadowflame → Rabadon's Deathcap, with Electrocute.
testPlan: Play it in mid as your control build. Follow the purchase order; the core (Stormsurge → Shadowflame → Rabadon's Deathcap) is what ranked players complete first.
Record kills, deaths, damage dealt and the minute you finish each core item, then compare other builds against these numbers in similar games.
Adapt the last two items to the enemy team: armor or magic resist against fed carries, anti-heal against healing, penetration once enemies stack resists.
failureConditions: Your results with this build fall clearly below the 51.9% ranked baseline over several games in the same role.
The enemy team composition makes the core items poor answers; swap the flexible slots before abandoning the core.
tradeoffs: Proven and predictable, so opponents know what to expect. It is a starting point, not the best build for every matchup.
The observed core and individual options do not establish six-item build statistics. Late slots are kit-based inferences.
Six-slot completion is our kit-based inference, not an observed six-item win-rate build.  Situational options replace an appropriate slot; they are not added as a seventh item.
buyOrder: Core in purchase order: Stormsurge → Shadowflame → Rabadon's Deathcap.
Boots after the first item unless the lane needs them earlier.
coverageNotes: Source: OP.GG ranked Emerald+ solo/duo, patch 16.20, checked 2026-10-14. Core items and rune page are observed; later slots are observed options or reviewed completions. Win rates describe those games, not a prediction for yours.
builds.author: Rift Build Lab ranked data

kitEvidence.formula:
Converge the realms, sending out a blast of spirit magic dealing [80 / 120 / 160 / 200 / 240 + (0.7) × AP] magic damage to enemies in the area and Slowing them by [80]% decaying over [1] second.

Aurora hops backwards a short distance after casting.

Damaging an enemy 3 times with Abilities or Attacks exorcises them, dealing [0.01 + (0.00027) × AP] max Health magic damage and, if the enemy is a champion, frees a spirit that follows Aurora for [4] seconds, restoring her Health for [characterLevelInterpolation(3 → 20; raw flags preserved) + (0.02) × AP] every second.

Leap in a direction. Upon landing, Aurora converges the realms, sending out a pulse of spirit energy that deals [175 / 275 / 375 + (0.7) × AP] magic damage and Slows enemies hit by [30]% for 2 seconds.

The area of convergence stays active for [3 / 3.5 / 4] seconds, granting Aurora Realm Hopper for [3.5 / 4.25 / 5] seconds, allowing her to jump from one edge of the area to another.

Enemies attempting to enter or leave the area are Slowed by [50]% for [1.5 / 1.75 / 2] seconds.

Aurora can Recast this Ability to end the effect early.

Fire cursed energy in a direction, dealing [45 / 70 / 95 / 120 / 145 + (0.4) × AP] magic damage to enemies and cursing them for [3.5] seconds.

Recast: End the curse, drawing back part of the enemy's spirit to Aurora, dealing up to [(45 / 70 / 95 / 120 / 145 + (0.4) × AP) × (1.5)] magic damage to enemies passed through based on their missing Health. Damage beyond the first hit is reduced to 20%.

If the duration runs out, Aurora will automatically Recast the Ability.

Hop in a direction. Upon landing, enter the spirit realm, becoming Invisible for [1 / 1.15 / 1.3 / 1.45 / 1.6] seconds and entering Realm Hopper, gaining [20 / 25 / 30 / 35 / 40]% Move Speed.

Scoring a takedown on an enemy champion resets this Ability's Cooldown.

builds.name: Spirit attack cycler
builds.summary: Test spirit attack cycler against the conventional damage pattern at equal gold.
builds.goal: Test spirit attack cycler against the conventional damage pattern at equal gold.
builds.hypothesis: Spirit Abjuration needs three attacks or ability hits and scales its max-health magic damage with AP; Nashor plus Dusk and Dawn helps fill the gaps between Twofold Hex passes. Riftmaker rewards staying through repeated spirit healing, while Bloodletter shreds MR through ability/passive magic damage.
testPlan: Required state: Use W invisibility to reset spacing, not abandon combat before procs.
Count exorcisms and healing in a moving ten-second chase.

Run three trials at matched level, ranks, gold and target defenses. Repeat against a moving opponent with a fixed incoming damage pattern. Record damage packets, missed actions, resource cost and survival separately.
Keep souls, health/mana, form, item/rune stacks, transformations and game time finite and explicitly recorded. No free full ramp or infinite scaling.
failureConditions: Short attack range and E's backward hop reduce actual attack uptime.
The narrow damage gain does not repay lost access, survival, wave control or allied utility.
tradeoffs: Rejected assumption: An extra item on-hit is not automatically another passive stack.
Confidence: plausible. Source-compatible reasoning is not in-game validation or proof of novelty/optimality.
buyOrder: Candidate six slots: Nashor's Tooth, Dusk and Dawn, Riftmaker, Bloodletter's Curse, Banshee's Veil, Berserker's Greaves. Compare two-item checkpoints before the final six-slot test; this list is not a lane shopping order.
Keep role-appropriate starters, boots and support quest/vision obligations. If the full candidate assumes farmed income, compare it separately from support income.
coverageNotes: Only Cassiopeia Q/E and Sett W have numerical adapters. Even there, these other objectives and item/rune interactions may fall outside the model.
Proc inheritance, crit, pet hits and conditional helpers remain uncertain until observed. No completed mathematical maximum is claimed.

builds.name: Situational adaptation: Survive the engage
builds.goal: Situational adaptation for Aurora: adapt to the specified fight rather than assume one universal build
builds.hypothesis: A mobile spell skirmisher who repeats hits to extract healing spirits and uses hops to adjust short-range pressure. Her ultimate creates a movement zone rather than guaranteeing enemies remain trapped. Do repeated spell hits extract enough spirits/healing to reward sustained AP rather than burst? Her R zone must be tested against targets that actually leave it. A transformed mana shield, stasis and a spell shield may preserve repeat casts.
builds.summary: A transformed mana shield, stasis and a spell shield may preserve repeat casts.
testPlan: Kit question for Aurora: Do repeated spell hits extract enough spirits/healing to reward sustained AP rather than burst? Her R zone must be tested against targets that actually leave it.

Start with the early core (Archangel, then the defense matching the opponent) plus appropriate boots at matched gold. Record level, actual ability ranks, forms, resource and item transformations; six-item results do not establish lane strength. Use your intended lane or jungle role; jungle starters and early consumables are outside the final six slots.

Compare against the reference route at the same level, gold spent, finite stacks and opponent setup. Record unused gold; isolate an item change before changing runes. Run three repeatable trials of a short trade and a ten-second fight. Record damage actually landed, attacks/casts, misses, remaining resource and survival. Record available/max mana and any transformed mana-item state.

Measure the actual interaction before granting item/rune procs: A transformed mana shield, stasis and a spell shield may preserve repeat casts. Test once stationary, then with a moving opponent and a fixed incoming damage pattern. Choose the opponent profile this defensive route is intended to address, then repeat against the wrong damage type.

Q evidence: Aurora sends out a missile that curses any enemies it hits. She can then recast the ability to draw active curses back toward herself, damaging foes who are hit along the way. Keep finite champion/item/rune stacks explicit. Use Practice Tool, a custom match or your own replay; no numerical adapter is available for this champion.
failureConditions: Defensive redundancy can sacrifice too much damage; this is conditional on real threats.

The route fails Aurora's stated kit question: Do repeated spell hits extract enough spirits/healing to reward sustained AP rather than burst? Her R zone must be tested against targets that actually leave it.
Higher dummy damage is offset by fewer landed actions, deaths before the useful window, or worse ally utility.
tradeoffs: Defensive redundancy can sacrifice too much damage; this is conditional on real threats.
Full cost 16,000 gold; delayed items, resource starvation and the two-item spike must be judged separately.
Counter-items are conditional. Change boots/defense for the real matchup, then record the modified setup.
buyOrder: Archangel, then the defense matching the opponent. Adapt component timing to lane/jungle pressure; do not blindly follow the displayed six-item order.
Keep appropriate boots while building the early core; swap boots only when the measured matchup justifies it.
Banshee's Veil, Rylai's Crystal Scepter, Void Staff are later or conditional slots; do not postpone necessary protection for a six-item ceiling.
Record available/max mana and any transformed mana-item state.
coverageNotes: No numerical damage or survival adapter exists for this champion. Loading this proposal opens a manual test sheet, not calculated damage.
Source formulas remain in Champion kit. Symbolic values, unresolved tokens and helper records are evidence to inspect, not a certified executable simulator.
Legal source item/rune references were checked; retained map flags cannot prove every live-shop condition. Confirm shop eligibility, exact on-hit/on-attack rules and real proc cooldowns in game.

builds.name: Realm healing endurance
builds.summary: Test realm healing endurance against the conventional damage pattern at equal gold.
builds.goal: Test realm healing endurance against the conventional damage pattern at equal gold.
builds.hypothesis: Between Worlds grants only three to four seconds of convergence; Cosmic Drive helps reposition for Q return and repeat Spirit Abjuration, while Visage increases received spirit healing. Liandry adds persistent magic pressure without asking basic attacks to carry the build.
testPlan: Required state: Enter with room for a Q return and multiple three-hit spirit cycles.
Compare spirit count and health remaining after ten seconds.

Run three trials at matched level, ranks, gold and target defenses. Repeat against a moving opponent with a fixed incoming damage pattern. Record damage packets, missed actions, resource cost and survival separately.
Keep souls, health/mana, form, item/rune stacks, transformations and game time finite and explicitly recorded. No free full ramp or infinite scaling.
failureConditions: Enemies leave the slow zone or burst her before Riftmaker matures.
The narrow damage gain does not repay lost access, survival, wave control or allied utility.
tradeoffs: Rejected assumption: The realm is not a permanent prison and takedown W resets are conditional.
Confidence: plausible. Source-compatible reasoning is not in-game validation or proof of novelty/optimality.
